title: HistoryPanel is a 3-D history container
summary: HistoryPanel holds shares × hdates × htypes; shape is (M, L, N). Use it to obtain, slice, rename, and restructure the panel—not to invent research factors or chart settings.
narrative:
HistoryPanel is qteasy's in-memory 3-D History container. The three axes are shares (symbols), hdates (time), and htypes (series names). shape is (M, L, N) for those axes in that order.

Only History-shaped series belong here. Macro and benchmarks stay on get_reference_data; industry and list_date stay on get_static_data. Obtain a panel with get_kline(..., as_panel=True) or get_history_data(..., as_data_frame=False). You can also build one for teaching with values, levels, rows, and columns.

Inspect with shares / hdates / htypes, print(hp), head/tail, and to_share_frame. Prefer subpanel, loc, and indexing over the deprecated slice / segment / isegment names. drop and rename change labels. Column access, assign, and simple expr add or rewrite columns as structure ops—they are not the research-factor lesson.

align_to enforces matching htypes before you merge two panels. Export with to_df_dict or MultiIndex helpers. Watch inplace defaults on fill helpers so you do not mutate a panel you still need.

This card does not teach returns, where masks, or hp.plot() parameters. Those are separate HistoryPanel topics.
python_code:
import qteasy as qt
hp = qt.get_kline(htypes='open, high, low, close, vol', shares='000300.SH', start='20230101', end='20230131', as_panel=True)
print(hp.shape, hp.shares, hp.htypes)
risk_notes: Reference and Static shapes are not panel axes. Adj names such as close|b are still History columns; look them up as DataTypes when unsure.
